paper_metadata.title: Neuropsychiatric sequelae one year after a minor head injury

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population and inclusion criteria. However, the authors admit that the ICD-9 search likely resulted in an incomplete list, and the final cohort represented only 48% of the expected eligible population in the district, suggesting potential selection bias toward more severe cases.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: All of these patients had a known address in the South Glamorgan Health District.
items.reasoning: The geographic and administrative source is clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The list was collected from the Health Authority's central data base by using the international classification of diseasesninth revision (ICD-9) codes10 and scrutinising medical case notes.
items.reasoning: While the method is described, the authors note in the discussion that the ICD-9 search likely yielded an incomplete list.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: admitted to hospital after a minor head injury between 1 July 1994 and 30 June 1995.
items.reasoning: Specific dates for the recruitment window are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: admitted to hospital... South Glamorgan Health District.
items.reasoning: The setting (hospital admission) and location are specified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The inclusion criteria were a Glasgow coma scale score between 13-159 and either a history of a period of lost consciousness after the head injury or radiological... or clinical evidence (focal neurological signs) of brain injury.
items.reasoning: Detailed clinical and radiological criteria are provided.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Our cohort included 48% (n=148) of all the expected patients with mild head injury who were admitted to a hospital.
items.reasoning: Participation is less than 50% of the expected eligible population, which is low and may introduce bias.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Patient's ages ranged between 18–93 years (median 39.5; quartile=27). There were 72 patients between the ages of 18 and 40 (51.4%)... Ninety three (66.4%) patients were men and 47 (33.6%) were women.
items.reasoning: Age and sex distributions are clearly reported.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study maintained a high follow-up rate (over 90% of the identified cohort) and provided reasons for those not interviewed.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Some data from medical notes were available on 140 patients, and 134 patients had a face to face interview.
items.reasoning: 134/148 (90.5%) completed the face-to-face interview, which is a high retention rate.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Those who did not respond initially received a reminder letter within 6 weeks, and again within 12 weeks... contacted by telephone or through their general practitioners (GPs).
items.reasoning: Multiple follow-up methods were employed to minimize attrition.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: Three patients were deceased at 1 year follow up... Eleven patients could not be contacted for an interview.
items.reasoning: Specific reasons (death, loss of contact) are listed.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not compare the characteristics of the 14 non-completers to the 134 completers.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no statistical comparison provided between completers and non-completers.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (age, GCS, alcohol, etc.) were measured using standardized tools or medical records consistently across the cohort.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Data were collected on the following areas: patient's age, sex, date of interview, date of head injury, and an estimate of current alcohol intake.
items.reasoning: The factors used in the regression analysis are explicitly listed.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: The data for the questionnaire were collected from patients' case notes and also from a face to face interview... Premorbid IQ was assessed by the national adult reading test (NART).
items.reasoning: Standardized tools (NART, MMSE) and medical records were used.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: A score <24 in the MMSE was taken as an evidence of overall cognitive deficit.
items.reasoning: Standard clinical cut-offs were used for continuous scales.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Two research staff (IL and CK) interviewed the patients and their relatives about 1 year after the head injury... primarily in their home settings.
items.reasoning: The protocol was standardized across the sample.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: 134 patients had a face to face interview.
items.reasoning: The majority of the cohort provided full data.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no mention of imputation; the study appears to use complete-case analysis.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes were measured using internationally recognized, validated scales (GOS, ERSS, CIS-R) administered by trained research staff.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Overall outcome at 1 year after head injury was assessed according to the Glasgow outcome scale12 and Edinburgh rehabilitation status scale (ERSS).
items.reasoning: The outcomes and the 1-year timeframe are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The CIS-R and PSQ... were shown to be reliable screening instruments for the detection of psychiatric cases in a general adult population.
items.reasoning: The study utilizes validated instruments with known psychometric properties.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Two research staff (IL and CK) interviewed the patients and their relatives about 1 year after the head injury.
items.reasoning: The assessment process was uniform for all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While multivariable regression was performed, the authors acknowledge that pre-existing disabilities (especially in the elderly) were not fully accounted for, which could confound the relationship between the head injury and 1-year outcomes.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: covariates: age, sex, average current weekly alcohol consumption, Glasgow coma scale score, NART score, history of a previous head injury, and MMSE score.
items.reasoning: Key demographic and injury variables were measured, but pre-injury psychiatric history or specific treatments were not explicitly included.
